chapter: Faith, Paris life and later years
title: Becoming a Muslim: praying to his Creator since age twelve
summary: He converted at the war's end but prays alone and does not attend mosque; since twelve he has invented his own prayers and called God his Creator.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

And you told me that this was shortly after the war. Well, you told me there was a man that you had been close to in the war --
-- that you had talked to. Well, so, then did you adopt the -- did you become a Muslim convert at the end of the war?
And then does that -- have you been a practicing Muslim ever since?
Well, I'll tell you, to a certain point, you know. I pray alone. I do everything alone.
-- things like -- I learned how to pray.
Yeah. In a way that appeals to me.
Yeah. Because prayer is a personal thing.
So I think that's the whole thing.

Because a lot of people, when I used to go to the Christian church when I was a kid, people would wear their best clothes and they would show off, and this and that, and it appeared to me that people just came to church just to show their new dress or their new pair of shoes they were wearing, and I didn't think that had anything to do with God at all.
You know? So I began to say prayers for myself, since I was 12 years old.

Yes. I never called God, God. I always called him my Creator.
So I said, well, the force that created me --
So there had to be some creation somewhere. So the Creator, I called God my Creator, and that's the end of it right there.
And he enters into your daily life, because --
-- the way you treat people, your friends --
-- everybody you love, you do that according to what you believe.
